worked_solution:
Since the Jordan block $J$ has a single $3\times 3$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =1,$ the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }{v}_{2}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ such that $(A-I){v}_{2}={v}_{1},$

- the third column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{3}$ such that $(A-I){v}_{3}={v}_{2}.$

Now, computing $A-I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-I){v}_{3}={v}_{2}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which is already in the row echelon form.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $2$nd and $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{2}+6\cdot (-1)=-4\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=2.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{1}=0,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $b+2c=2+2\cdot (-1)=0.$
